kwargs.profile_path: required: the profile directory (profile['path'] in audit_surface._sweep). The module reads <profile>/config.yaml itself for every config-derived value below; no credential file is opened.
kwargs.memory_char_limit: omit (recommended): read from <profile>/config.yaml key memory.memory_char_limit; missing config.yaml or missing key => shipped default 2200 (hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:1304); unreadable config, duplicate keys, ${...} values, non-positive or non-integer values, or an active managed overlay (/etc/hermes, HERMES_MANAGED_DIR; same rule as write_settings) => unknown. Explicit None => unknown; explicit int => caller value.
kwargs.user_char_limit: omit (recommended): config.yaml memory.user_char_limit, default 1375 (hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:1305); same rules as memory_char_limit.
kwargs.memory_provider: omit (recommended): config.yaml memory.provider (agent/agent_init.py:1254-1278); missing => no external provider. Explicit None => no external provider; explicit string => caller value. Only byterover/retaindb/other is emitted, never the name.
kwargs.home_os: omit (recommended): the host OS from sys.platform (linux/macos/windows), correct for the live home the audit inspects. Explicit None => unknown (other-OS measurements null, coverage could_not_verify).
kwargs.prompt_injecting_plugins: caller: list of enabled plugin names whose manifest declares pre_llm_call or pre_gateway_dispatch. The module does not read plugin manifests; the matching data is computed by audit/unattended_exposure.py (PROMPT_INJECTING_HOOKS, around lines 1592 and 1944). Omitted/None => unknown (coverage could_not_verify). Names are only counted and deduplicated, never emitted. The caller either passes that list from unattended_exposure or passes [] and accepts the limitation.
kwargs.project_families: caller: dict mapping technology family labels (audit.session_contamination families, e.g. 'python') to counts for the selected/registered projects; audit.session_contamination._project(root) returns the family set per project root (call it for each p['canonical_path'] in projects or inventory['project_units'], as the session_contamination call does). Omitted/None => no projects to compare with: only the foreign-technology sub-check is skipped (foreign-technology measurements null, foreign_technology_coverage could_not_verify, foreign_technology_reason no_projects); the section itself can still be verified. Any other value that is not a dict of strings => unknown (section coverage could_not_verify, truncated_by input_unknown, foreign_technology_reason input_unknown). Keys are never emitted.
kwargs.clock: omit: time.monotonic. Used only for the five-second budget and run_metrics.elapsed_ms.

consequences.memory_load.could_not_verify: Some memory measurements could not be verified; missing coverage is not a clean result.
consequences.memory_load.duplicate_entries: Normalized entries or eight-word shingles were counted that repeat within or across live memory files; the count does not show that the repeated text means the same thing.
consequences.memory_load.foreign_technology_entries: Entries were counted that name technology families absent from the supplied projects; the count does not show that those entries are irrelevant.
consequences.memory_load.limit_raised_above_shipped: The character limit for a memory file is set above the value Hermes ships with; text in these files is sent with every request, so a higher limit allows more text on every request. The setting was measured from config.yaml and does not show who changed it or why.
consequences.memory_load.memory_state_sprawl: A memory state directory, found by name and counted by file metadata only, holds more than 100 files; the count does not show whether the files are used or repeat each other.
consequences.memory_load.mostly_dated_entries: Memory files were counted where more than half of at least six entries contain a calendar date; a date does not show that the entry is out of date.
consequences.memory_load.multiple_memory_systems: Two or more memory mechanisms are configured or present together; the audit counted them from config and files, and did not measure what each adds to a request or whether they repeat each other.
consequences.memory_load.other_machine_entries: Memory files were counted whose entries contain another operating system's home-path form or a private-network address; this is left over text from another machine, and the count does not show that it is used or wrong here.
consequences.memory_load.over_limit: Memory files (live or snapshot copies) are longer, in characters, than the character limit used for this audit; this compares file length only and does not measure what is sent with a request.
consequences.memory_load.pending_edit_changes_approva: This counts pending memory edits where an edit replaces or removes an entry that contains approval-related words; it is a word count and does not show that any approval setting or instruction would change.
consequences.memory_load.stale_pending_edits: Pending memory edits were counted whose old text is absent from the current target file; the count does not predict whether approving them would succeed.
consequences.memory_load.standing_orders: Entries phrased as always/never instructions were counted by word match; the count does not show who wrote them, whether they are followed, or whether they are wrong.

notes: Envelope: make_component_envelope(findings, coverage, extra={'memory_load': section, 'run_metrics': {...}}), the same shared builder write_settings uses; it also carries ok/error/classification. adapt_component_result recomputes classification, normalizes coverage (forced to could_not_verify when any finding is could_not_verify), drops ok/status/error/classification (legacy 'pass' is kept as legacy_status_ignored) and copies every other top-level key, so memory_load AND run_metrics both survive as siblings (tested).

run_metrics = {'elapsed_ms': int} from the injected clock. It must NOT be placed in store.finalize_run measurements or anything digested; the section and findings are byte-identical for runs with clocks days apart (tested).

free_strings is empty: the section and findings emit only numbers, booleans, nulls and the vocabulary above. No memory text, entry hashes, profile/plugin/provider names, paths, stamps or ids are emitted (canary tests over every input).

Shared-set additions this section needs: 58 schema keys, 23 vocabulary tokens, 2 numeric evidence keys (mechanisms, builtin_nonempty), 11 rule ids, 11 consequence sentences (none currently allowed). Without them the serializer turns unknown dict keys into hmac SealedKeys, unknown string values into hashed 'text' tokens, finding_dto seals the unknown rule id as a hash, replaces every consequence with DEFAULT_FINDING_CONSEQUENCE and drops mechanisms/builtin_nonempty from evidence (tested by test_unsealed_sets_would_drop_memory_load_output, which skips once the sets are added).

Wiring: in audit_surface._sweep (full_home branch only) call _component('memory_load', identity, memory_load.audit_memory_load, profile_path=profile['path'], prompt_injecting_plugins=..., project_families=...); add 'memory_load' to the measurements dict and to the name tuple in audit/store.py finalize_run (currently skill_hygiene/write_settings/session_contamination only).

Caller inputs: prompt_injecting_plugins and project_families are the only inputs the module cannot derive itself. Plugin hook declarations are parsed by audit/unattended_exposure.py (PROMPT_INJECTING_HOOKS); project families by audit.session_contamination._project. prompt_injecting_plugins not passed => the section stays coverage could_not_verify with truncated_by input_unknown, and multiple_memory_systems omits them. project_families not passed => only the foreign-technology sub-check is skipped (foreign_technology_reason no_projects).

config.yaml is read with fingerprint.safe_read_regular_file + facts._parse_simple_yaml_mapping (reject duplicate keys) and the write_settings managed-overlay rule; inside a run this is the same capture-cached read write_settings already makes. Memory files themselves never enter the shared capture (private descriptor-relative reader).

time_budget: on a very slow filesystem the five-second cooperative budget can cut a scan, so truncated_by/coverage may differ between runs; this is coverage-marked, not wall-clock data in the section.

README disclosure needed (from the module review): reads memory snapshot files under backups/memory-bg-review if present (backups/memory-bg-review/<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>/<hex id>/{MEMORY,USER}.md in the main home only).

memlock / memory-lock / memory_lock are the state directory names of a third-party memory plugin (module constant STATE_DIR_NAMES); they are data and are emitted only as stores[].name labels. memory-lock and memory_lock appear only when such a directory exists.

char_limits.{memory,user}: shipped_char_limit (module DEFAULT_MEMORY_LIMIT/DEFAULT_USER_LIMIT = hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:1304-1305, 2200/1375), configured_char_limit (resolved limit, null when unknown), limit_ratio_to_shipped (configured/shipped rounded to 2 decimals, null when unknown), limit_source (the input_sources token: config/default/caller/could_not_verify), chars_over_shipped_limit (main-home file characters beyond the shipped limit, 0 when under or absent, null when unmeasured). memory_load.limit_raised_above_shipped fires only when a limit FROM config.yaml is strictly greater than shipped (review_suggested when a raised ratio >= 2.0, else info); a caller limit, an equal/lower limit or an unknown limit gives no finding. Evidence is numeric only: <kind>_shipped_char_limit, <kind>_configured_char_limit, <kind>_limit_ratio_to_shipped (float), <kind>_characters; unknown values are left out.

Reason codes outside the scan cuts (TRUNCATION_REASONS) also appear in truncated_by and are not counted in limits.cuts: input_unknown (a setting the check needs could not be read: config.yaml unreadable or ambiguous, provider, limits, host system or plugin list unknown) and missing (the profile folder was not found). foreign_technology_reason is null when the sub-check ran, else no_projects or input_unknown.
